title: Captain Bee's Diary
subtitle: An unmarked treasure trail in Skyline Valley

sections.title: Finding Them
sections.html:
There are 6 pages of Bee's Diary and 1 final note in Skyline Valley. Each one is a fixed spawn, so it's always in the same place.

  • Check the map. Maps, at the bottom of the page, has every spot marked if you'd rather skip the directions.
  • Follow the statues. At pages 1 to 5, a Steel Jack statue points at the spot where the page is hidden. Stand on or in front of it and look where it's pointing.
  • Go in order. Nothing locks the pages to an order, but each page hints at the next spot, so the story reads best from page 1 to 6.
  • No quest marker. There's no quest and nothing in your Pip-Boy tracks it: you just find the pages.
  • Where they go. The pages go in the Notes tab of your Pip-Boy.

sections.title: How to Start the Trail
sections.html:
There's nothing to start, because Captain Bee's Diary has no quest. Fast travel to Shenandoah Visitor Center and find the first Steel Jack statue (Step 1 below).

{img:/wp-content/uploads/guide-images/quests/secrets-and-easter-eggs/captain-bees-diary/shenandoah-visitor-center.avif}

sections.title: Captain Bee's Diary Walkthrough
sections.html:
Step 1 – Find the Steel Jack statue at Shenandoah Visitor Center

From the fast travel point, run into the car park and stop at the tree in the middle. Face east towards the Visitor Center: the statue is on your right.

{img:/wp-content/uploads/guide-images/quests/secrets-and-easter-eggs/captain-bees-diary/steel-jack-1-shenandoah-visitor-center.avif}

Step 2 – Take page 1 from the First Aid box

Climb onto the statue and look the way it points. Page 1 is in the First Aid box on the bathroom wall.

{img:/wp-content/uploads/guide-images/quests/secrets-and-easter-eggs/captain-bees-diary/page-1-first-aid-box.avif}
Bee's Diary page 1

October 18th 2077

First day on the job and I'm left with the last guy's mess. The park is in such disrepair, I've really got my work cutout for me. It's gonna take me the whole year... NO... maybe longer to get everything up to standard, and don't get me started with the Steel Jack statues, they're first on my list of work. I wonder what they're always pointing at?

Whilst leaving my room this morning I noticed an interesting trail off to the side of the Slumber Mill to explore. I think I might have to sneak off tomorrow and see where it leads.

Step 3 – Find the statue near High Knob Lookout

Fast travel to High Knob Lookout. Head north down the path, keeping right, until you reach the main road. Go left along the road to the red, rusty pick-up truck on your right, turn right there and follow the path to the end, then go up the stairs to the statue.

{img:/wp-content/uploads/guide-images/quests/secrets-and-easter-eggs/captain-bees-diary/steel-jack-2-high-knob-lookout.avif}

Step 4 – Take page 2 from the Hollow Stump

Stand in front of the statue and look where it points. Go back down the stairs, face north and walk slowly forward: the big stump is on your left, half hidden in the bushes.

{img:/wp-content/uploads/guide-images/quests/secrets-and-easter-eggs/captain-bees-diary/page-2-hollow-stump.avif}
Bee's Diary Page 2

October 19th 2077

During my little "break" today, I had a venture down the trail. I didn't have a lot of time before they noticed I had snuck off, really got an earful about that.

I came across a really cute tree stump with shrooms growing all over it. I had a little rest there before I got radioed back. I'll try and cover more ground tomorrow.

Step 5 – Find the statue near Naked Creek

Fast travel to Naked Creek. Take the path east to the road, turn right and follow it down to the pick-up truck and trailer. Face north and you'll see a dirt path going up the hill. Take the left fork and keep going all the way to the top: it's a long climb.

{img:/wp-content/uploads/guide-images/quests/secrets-and-easter-eggs/captain-bees-diary/steel-jack-3-naked-creek.avif}

Step 6 – Take page 3 from the Hollow Stump

Climb onto the statue and look the way it points. The stump is just behind a corpse.

{img:/wp-content/uploads/guide-images/quests/secrets-and-easter-eggs/captain-bees-diary/page-3-hollow-stump.avif}
Bee's Diary Page 3

October 20th 2077

God damn I really got chewed out for disappearing yesterday, everyone's so stressed over the delivery of the new Steel Jack statue. I've told them a thousand times, the boardwalk is too heavy to hold a 3000 pound statue, especially in a swamp of all places.

I went back to my favorite trail to hide away from all the stress. I ventured a little further today. I followed the old wooden fencing until it reached a small rocky pass with a beautiful tree splitting the road. It was a peaceful place to have lunch. I'll try and go there again tomorrow.

Step 7 – Find the statue at Old Rag Lookout

From the fast travel point, face south-east and follow the path with the wooden railings. Where it splits at the wood pile, take the right-hand path and follow it to the end.

{img:/wp-content/uploads/guide-images/quests/secrets-and-easter-eggs/captain-bees-diary/steel-jack-4-old-rag-lookout.avif}

Step 8 – Take page 4 from the Hollowed-Out Rock

Climb onto the statue and look the way it points. The rock is at the edge of the picnic area, past the picnic benches.

{img:/wp-content/uploads/guide-images/quests/secrets-and-easter-eggs/captain-bees-diary/page-4-hollowed-out-rock.avif}
Bee's Diary Page 4

October 21st 2077

Chief Pilker has his stooges Hailey and Matthews keeping tabs on me. He said I should be spending all my time doing my job and that the park is too dangerous to be just disappearing without letting anyone know.

So I managed to lose the dopes. I continued along the path until I found a trail leading off to the right. I found an absolute gem, a rocky overview, I can even see the camp from here. With a little bit of fixing up I can spend all my lunches resting here.

Step 9 – Find the statue near Abandoned Convoy

From the fast travel point, face north-west and run until you reach a small hiking sign. Bear right and follow the hiking path west. Cross the first bridge, then turn left where the second bridge starts and follow the path to the end.

{img:/wp-content/uploads/guide-images/quests/secrets-and-easter-eggs/captain-bees-diary/steel-jack-5-abandoned-convoy.avif}

Step 10 – Take page 5 from the Duffle Bag

Climb onto the statue and walk the way it points. Jump off the bridge and keep going straight through the water until you reach a big white tree. The bag sits in the fork of the tree, so climb up to reach it.

{img:/wp-content/uploads/guide-images/quests/secrets-and-easter-eggs/captain-bees-diary/page-5-duffle-bag.avif}
Bee's Diary Page 5

October 22nd 2077

The Steel Jack statue was installed today, what a disaster. How many times do I have to say a poorly built wooden walkway can only carry so much and then plop, straight into the swamp water.

I finished work early today, borrowed one of the ranger's utility cars to transport some bits to fix up the trail leading to the overview to make it more comfortable. I've hidden a small trinket cache in a stump next to the resting area, and marked it with an axe. I plan on hiding my past few diary entries around the park, maybe it will inspire more adventurers to explore this place.

Step 11 – Take page 6 from the stump with the axe

There's no statue for this one. From the South River Bridge fast travel point, head south across the river (three Firecaps grow on the far bank) and keep going south until you reach a hiking path. Follow it uphill; there are enemies at the top. Stand on the second picnic table on your left, face south and walk to the Bear Proof bin: the stump with an axe in it is on your left, behind a rock. Page 6 is inside.

{img:/wp-content/uploads/guide-images/quests/secrets-and-easter-eggs/captain-bees-diary/page-6-hollow-stump-axe.avif}
Bee's Diary Page 6

Congratulations!!

You've found captain Bee's treasure and this wonderful overlook. Claim your prize and always keep adventuring!

Step 12 – Find Bee's Final Note

Stand with the axe stump behind you and face east. Walk to the path, then turn west: the note is on the ground beside a skeleton.

{img:/wp-content/uploads/guide-images/quests/secrets-and-easter-eggs/captain-bees-diary/final-note-skeleton.avif}
Bee's Final Note

The ground shook so hard knocking me over, and as if my luck could get any worse, the god damn tree pinned my legs.

I can't believe I'm saying this, but I should have listened to the Chief. I hope someone finds me soon, I'm so hungry and cold.

sections.title: Rewards
sections.html:
There's no quest reward and no plan. Every container holds its own loot as well as the diary page:

1Shenandoah Visitor CenterFirst AidMedkit loot
2High Knob LookoutHollow StumpCaps stash (medium), Medkit loot
3Naked CreekHollow StumpMedkit loot, Toolbox loot
4Old Rag LookoutHollowed-Out Rock3× RadAway, Bubblegum, 3× Stimpak

Bee's Final Note lies on the ground by the skeleton, so there's nothing else with it.

sections.title: FAQ and Important Info
sections.html:
Do I have to find the pages in order?

No. Each page is in its own container and nothing checks the order. Going from page 1 to 6 just makes the story easier to follow.

Is there a plan at the end?

No. None of the containers has a plan, and finishing the trail doesn't give anything extra.

Why isn't it in my Pip-Boy quests?

It isn't a quest. It's a hidden trail made to get people exploring Skyline Valley.

Does the Steel Jack statue turn up anywhere else?

Yes. The statue on the Naked Creek trail is also a stop in Event: Mischief Night, where JES-2R leads you to it.

sections.title: Lore
sections.html:
Bee started work as a park ranger in Skyline Valley on 18 October 2077. The park was run down, the Steel Jack statues were first on the to-do list, and Bee kept wondering what they were all pointing at.

Over the next few days Bee kept sneaking off along a trail near the Slumber Mill: to a stump covered in mushrooms, then a rocky pass split by a tree, then a rocky overlook with a view of the camp. Chief Pilker didn't like it and had Hailey and Matthews keep an eye on Bee, but Bee lost them.

Bee had also warned everyone that the boardwalk couldn't hold a 3,000-pound Steel Jack statue in a swamp. On 22 October it went in, and straight into the water. That afternoon Bee hid a small cache in a stump marked with an axe near the overlook, and planned to hide the diary pages around the park to get people exploring.

The diary stops there, the day before the bombs fell. Bee's Final Note, by a skeleton a few steps from the axe stump, tells the rest: the ground shook, a tree pinned Bee's legs, and Bee wished they had listened to the Chief.
